summary: Former BC fire lookout north of Revelstoke, reached by boat and a 5.5 km overgrown service road; no build or staffing history in the sources read.

facts.status_note: Firelookout.ca calls it a former BC Fire Lookout; no source read says whether the tower still stands.

visit.trail_note: 5.5 km (3.4 mi) one-way hike along an overgrown lookout tower service road, reached by a branch of the Wood River Forest Service Road and a boat ride across Kinbasket Lake.

evidence.supports: Location north of Revelstoke and west of Cummins Lakes Provincial Park
evidence.quote: North of Revelstoke and west of Cummins Lakes Provincial Park

evidence.supports: Access by a branch of the Wood River FSR and boat across Kinbasket Lake
evidence.quote: can be accessed off a branch of the Wood River Forest Service Road, which in turn is accessed by boat ride across Kinbasket Lake

evidence.supports: 5.5 km one-way hike along an overgrown service road
evidence.quote: From the road, it is a 5.5 km (3.4 mi) one-way hike along an overgrown lookout tower service road to the top.

evidence.supports: Elevation gain figures that do not agree with each other
evidence.quote: Expect an elevation gain of 1,060 m (5,250 ft) from the road, or 1,600 m (5,250 ft) in total.

evidence.supports: Index files the site under a Bulkley - Nechako label
Near Kinbasket Lake; status uncertain; access difficult
evidence.quote: Cummins (near Kinbasket Lake — status uncertain, access difficult)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The web index files Cummins Mountain under Bulkley - Nechako, but Firelookout.ca places the lookout north of Revelstoke. The story reports both without choosing one.
Firelookout.ca gives two climb figures, 1,060 m and 1,600 m, each paired with 5,250 ft, so they cannot both match the feet figure. The story reports the disagreement without choosing a number.

sources.title: Cummins Mountain
sources.publisher: Canada Lookouts (web index of Canadian lookouts)

sources.title: Fire Lookouts of British Columbia: History, Hikes & Where to Stay

notes_for_editor: No build date, builder, staffing or fire history was found in readable sources. A BC Archives record whose title refers to a forest lookout on Cummins Mountain turned up in search, but both fetch_text (SSL error) and WebFetch (certificate error) failed on it, so it is not used and may hold the build history. Firelookout.ca's lookout pages load their data by script; only the description text from the source page was readable, and it has no build or height fields. Wild Bluebell is a travel blog and is weighted low. No access level is recorded because no source says whether the site is public, only that access is difficult. No photos. The Facebook group posts were not read.
